subject: Biology

nodes.text: light provides the energy that drives the reaction
chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves, absorbs the light energy
the plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air through tiny pores called stomata
water is absorbed from the soil by the roots and carried to the leaves
carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose, a sugar that stores chemical energy as the plant's food
oxygen is released into the air as a byproduct
the reaction takes place inside chloroplasts in the leaf cells

textbookPhrasings: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesise food from carbon dioxide and water.
In the presence of chlorophyll and sunlight, carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose and oxygen.
Photosynthesis is a physiological process in which light energy is converted into chemical energy stored in glucose.
referenceFacts: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air
Oxygen is released as a byproduct of photosynthesis
Glucose is produced and stores chemical energy
Water is absorbed by the roots from the soil
Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts of leaf cells
Light energy is converted into chemical energy

whyQuestions.q: Why can't photosynthesis happen in the dark?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: light supplies the energy that powers the reaction, so without light there is no energy source

whyQuestions.q: Why do plants need chlorophyll specifically, and not just any colour?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: chlorophyll is the pigment that actually absorbs light energy and passes it into the reaction

whyQuestions.q: Why is photosynthesis important for animals like us?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: it releases the oxygen we breathe and creates the food energy at the base of the food chain

misconceptions: Plants get their food from the soil
Plants breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide during photosynthesis
Chlorophyll is the food that plants make
